glossUnihan: the passive, female principle in Chinese philosophy (yin); dark; secret
formNote: The Shuowen: 陰，闇也。水之南、山之北也 — “dark: the south bank of a river, the north slope of a hill.” Mojidata IDS: ⿰阝侌.
summary: The shady side of a hill: from a word of landscape, yin became half of the pair that runs through Chinese cosmology, medicine and divination. It is the dark, the receptive, the cool; never alone, always with 陽.
placement: Just above the centre, on the left, facing 陽 across the axis. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Shady Slope
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen: 陰，闇也。水之南、山之北也. Yin is first a place: the south bank of a river and the north slope of a hill, both out of the sun. The cosmology grew from a way of reading terrain.

satellites.title: The Way of Yin and Yang in Japan
satellites.evidence: In Japan the court discipline of calendars, divination and protection was 陰陽道, onmyōdō. Unihan’s Japanese readings give 陰 on and 陽 yō; in the compound they join as on-myō, by sound linking (連声).
satellites.caveat: The sound-linking explanation and the history of onmyōdō are Baracus’s, from general knowledge; only the readings are checked.
